key_insight: WorldWeaver (W²) shifts multi-agent video generation from simply carrying forward past observations to maintaining persistent shared world state across agents and views. This helps generated scenes stay consistent over time, even when multiple agents interact or the viewpoint changes.
problem_solved: Existing autoregressive video diffusion models struggle to preserve a common world state in multi-agent and multi-view settings because they condition mainly on observation history. That makes it hard to keep objects, interactions, and scene state coherent across agents and across rolling generations.
method: Introduces a streaming multi-agent autoregressive diffusion framework for video generation.
Augments rollout with cross-agent world state registers to store persistent shared state beyond local observation history.
Uses these registers to propagate consistent information across agents and viewpoints as the world evolves.
impact: This approach could improve interactive simulation, embodied AI, multi-agent planning, and generative world modeling by making long-horizon scene continuity more reliable. For practitioners, it points toward a better way to model shared environment state in complex, dynamic settings.
